message: Sleeping under 6 hours is linked to more of me the next day, which can feel like being wired but tired.
I build up while you are awake and clear during sleep. After a short night some of me is left over, which is linked to sleepiness and lower energy.
A full night of sleep supports my normal rhythm: high in the morning to wake you up, low at night.
Caffeine works by blocking me, the molecule that makes you sleepy. More than 2 cups, especially late in the day, is linked to taking longer to fall asleep.
A lot of caffeine is linked to short-term rises in me, which can feel like jitters or anxiety.
High anxiety goes with an active fight-or-flight response, where I raise your heart rate and alertness. Slow breathing and a short walk help your body settle.
I'm your brain's calming signal. Sleep and exercise are linked to me working well, so both are worth protecting on anxious days.
Daylight is linked to my activity. You logged under 20 minutes outdoors; a short walk in daylight may help your mood.
Your skin makes me from sunlight. Little time outdoors, especially in winter, is linked to lower vitamin D.
Days are short where you are right now. Morning light helps set the body clock that times me, so try to get outside early in the day.
30 minutes or more of movement today. Exercise is linked to me being released, and to better motivation and mood.
Regular movement is linked to more of my activity. Even 10 minutes of walking counts.
Low mood and low motivation are linked with my signalling and serotonin's, together with sleep, stress and life events. One low day is normal. If it lasts two weeks or more, talk to a GP.
Very low energy usually has everyday causes such as sleep. We set the pace of your metabolism, so tiredness that lasts for weeks is worth mentioning to a GP.
I carry oxygen in your blood, and low iron is linked to tiredness. Skipping meals makes it harder to get enough of me.
I support your blood and nerve cells, and low B12 is linked to tiredness and low mood. I come from regular meals with animal products or fortified foods.
You took vitamin D today. Supplements are one way to keep my levels up when there is little sun. Stay within the dose on the label.
